evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities repeatedly emphasize data quality, metric governance, documentation, lineage, and testing/validation with no velocity/speed language present, placing this at rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: Establish and maintain strong metadata, documentation, lineage, and semantic consistency for analytics datasets and reporting layers,
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect internal KPI reporting and business decision-making at an e-commerce/retail company without financial-reporting or regulatory-audit language, placing this at moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing BI/Data Engineering function with established reporting tools (Tableau, Power BI) and enterprise data architecture is already in place and being extended, indicating a growing but already-established data function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Support KPI setup and metric governance by aligning definitions, calculation logic, metadata, and reporting standards across different business domains,
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name specific practices (KPI governance, semantic models, metadata/lineage, dimensional modeling) but are largely generic BI/analytics-engineering boilerplate that could describe many similar roles, characteristic of a role written with broad applicability rather than sharp specificity.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Work closely with BI, Data Engineering, and business stakeholders to understand reporting requirements and translate them into scalable analytics data solutions,
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on building the internal data/reporting layer that BI, Data Engineering, and business stakeholders broadly consume, an internal-data orientation rather than one specific commercial, product, or finance function.
evidence.autonomy_level: Design, build, and maintain analytics-ready datasets, transformation logic, and semantic models to support dashboards, KPI reporting, and business analysis,
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: All responsibilities are scoped execution verbs (design, build, maintain, develop, support, monitor, participate) responding to defined reporting requirements rather than setting new strategic direction.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tooling or AI-adjacent responsibility is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Participate in release planning, testing, validation, and cross-functional coordination for analytics changes to ensure reporting quality and business continuity.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and validation are framed as an owned responsibility with explicit ownership language (participate, ensure), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Monitor and troubleshoot data quality issues, model performance, and reporting inconsistencies, and drive timely resolution and continuous improvement,
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data quality, consistency, and reporting reliability are named as ongoing secondary concerns without regulatory or stakeholder-trust framing dominating the JD, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Improve analytics development efficiency through reusable frameworks, standardized modeling approaches, and best practices in data transformation and version control,
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by maintain/improve/standardize verbs applied to existing analytics infrastructure rather than building new systems from scratch, indicating fix/scale.
